method.title: How it’s calculated
method.how: Each measure is compared with people your age (and sex for physical tests) in Canada and the United States: 12-minute run converted to VO2max (FRIEND registry), push-ups (Canadian Society for Exercise Physiology), sit-and-reach (YMCA), bench press relative to body weight (Cooper Institute), squats and standing long jump; net income per hour (Census Bureau), net worth (Federal Reserve and Statistics Canada) and savings rate (Federal Reserve). A measure is at level 25 when it beats 25% of people your age. A pillar is at the level of its weakest measure: to level up, each measure must reach the next threshold, and those are your level goals.
method.elite: From 90 to 100, the elite zone goes from the 90th percentile up to the human peak for your age: world-class athletes for physical tests, the richest 0.1% of your age group for finances.
method.limits: Limits: squats, the jump, the bench press and the elite zone rely on estimates (marked “Estimate”); your answers are self-reported, not verified; hourly income for Canada uses the US curve.
method.notice: Automated decision (Québec Law 25): your level is calculated by the app from your measures, never by AI. You can redo a measure to correct it, or erase everything.

benchSteps.title: How to do the bench press test
benchSteps.warmUp: Warm up: one set of 10 with the empty bar, then one set of 5 with a light weight.
benchSteps.choose: Pick a heavy weight you can lift between 1 and 10 times with good form.
benchSteps.lift: Lying on the bench with your feet on the floor, lower the bar until it touches your chest, then press until your arms are straight. Don’t bounce it off your chest.
benchSteps.count: Do as many reps as you can in a row, without resting, and stop when your form breaks.
benchSteps.write: Enter your body weight, the total weight and the number of reps. Get iT estimates your one-rep max and compares it to your weight.
benchSteps.example: Example: 87 kg body weight, 100 kg lifted 3 times → about 110 kg for one rep, 1.26 times your weight.
benchSteps.safety: Always with a spotter or on a machine. Never test your max alone.
